agents.reasoning: Started from the approved quarterly driver set (kept exactly; my disagreements are in gap_note) and looked for what makes consensus wrong on the downside. Evidence found: (1) insiders sold ~$1.09B of stock May-Oct 2026 across 90 Form 4s with no open-market purchase (Slootman $731M, Dageville $175M, Speiser $85M, Kleinerman $46M, Garrett $43M) [25,30]; mostly 10b5-1 and founder/director diversification, so a weak signal on fundamentals but a steady supply overhang. (2) Credit: $3.75B 0% converts (conversion ~500/484, capped calls to 820.30, cost 383.5) plus ~286M premium to retire 261.8 of 2027 notes [10,26]; principal now 5.79B vs 7.10B cash, so the balance sheet is fine (net cash 1.31B) but the cash is no longer 'excess', and the 2027/2029 notes are in the money (~10M shares in the guide). No covenant or rating issue. (3) Litigation: four unaccrued matters (two 10b-5 suits, breach MDL with standing upheld, LLM copyright class) [7,27,32]; small in expected value (~-0.2/share). (4) Accounting/quality: GAAP operating loss TTM -1,237M [F13] with SBC 1,642M [F46]; FCF less SBC is negative (-447M TTM); the Q2 FY27 'new customer' residual jump (7.9% of product revenue) includes Observe/Natoma acquisitions and TTM lag; cRPO covers only ~69% of the set's NTM product revenue and total RPO fell 9.77B -> 9.00B since Q4 FY26 [7], so the NRR path rests on uncontracted on-demand consumption. (5) Competition: Databricks >$7B run-rate, >80% growth, SQL warehousing >$1.5B >100% [28]; Iceberg flagged by the company itself as reducing lock-in [7]. Weighed honestly: the beat record (10/10 product and margin) and AI consumption acceleration are real, and none of the bear items is a smoking gun; the downside case is mostly a multiple story. Valuation: EV/sales is the only multiple that works with GAAP losses (METHOD FIT weakens GAAP P/E and EV/EBITDA, which I do not use, and partly EV/sales because it ignores SBC), so I added a 10%-weight SBC-burdened earnings-power leg (99).
